title: “They Say in the School of Rav”
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 17b they said that wherever it says “they say in the school of Rav,” it is Rav Huna; and it is objected: “But did not Rav Huna say, ‘They say in the school of Rav’? Rather (it is) Rav Hamnuna.” Hyman considers both attributions correct and reconstructs the history as follows. When Rav died, the academy of Sura remained without a head out of respect for Shmuel, who remained the teacher of the whole Diaspora in Nehardea, and all of Rav’s great students came to study before Shmuel. But the academy of Sura was not abolished, and there was there a gathering of sages whose leader was Rav Hamnuna, as explained in his entry, and they sent all their doubts to Shmuel, as we find in Gittin 66b and 89a, Bava Batra 152b, Sanhedrin 24b and Shevuot 46a: “They sent from the school of Rav to Shmuel: Let our master teach us.” And when the students stated a halakhah in Rav’s name, it was said — Shabbat 85a, Eruvin 89b and 94b, Yevamot 83a — “They say in the school of Rav in Rav’s name”; and Hyman considers that this was certainly said by Rav’s great students, such as Rav Huna, who reigned after Shmuel’s death. So too we find in Berakhot 3a, “Rav Ada bar Ahavah said: They say in the school of Rav,” and he was one of Rav’s great students. But we also find in Zevachim 87a, “They say in the school of Rav: What is Rav Chisda’s reason?” and there the reference is to the study house.

notes.text: Hyman reconciles the Huna/Hamnuna attributions through his academy-history reconstruction; this is not a global formula-to-person binding. His certainly assertion and the later generic study-house sense remain attributed and distinct.

Sanhedrin 17b directly gives the Huna proposal, objection and Hamnuna answer. The subsequent reconciliation through Sura’s academy history and the certainty attached to Rav’s senior students are Hyman’s reconstruction, not a universal assignment of the formula to one person.
